svg.text: The map before the journey, and the only questions worth asking directly
Long flows die from uncertainty, not length. The road map costs one screen and turns every screen after it into progress. What follows are capacity questions — facts the user already
How much are you starting with?
How much can you add each month?
For how long do you want to invest?
How much you are starting with, how much you can add each month, how long you want to leave it. Facts and intentions the user can state without introspection — unlike “how would you feel
about a 20% drop,” which nobody can answer honestly. The goal chosen at the start governs what else gets asked: a travel plan asks where and for how long; a retirement plan doesn't.
The flow has distinct modes — answering about your money, being measured on risk, receiving results. A short screen sits between each, so the user knows the nature of the task has changed instead
One screen of orientation buys four phases of patience.
